title: Replace synchronous logger with async journaling and introduce span coalescer to cut tail latency
creator: Alex Chen
description:
Problem: Several production incidents and long-tail latency traces point to synchronous logging flush and high-span-churn in the OpenTelemetry exporter as primary contributors to p99 spikes during bursty workloads. Our current sync logger forces request threads to block on I/O during log/metric emission; the OTLP exporter currently emits individual spans immediately which increases network overhead and amplifies per-request latency under backpressure.

Goal: Replace the synchronous logging path in the runtime with an async journal (in-memory ring buffer + background writer) and add a span coalescer/batcher inside the OTLP exporter to reduce per-request allocations and network calls. This should reduce p99 tail latency, lower CPU spent in logging, and reduce cardinality and egress cost for telemetry.

Scope: runtime-serving binary and the in-process telemetry adapter (Go). Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK to v1.19.x to pick up batching improvements and stable APIs, but keep shim compatibility for older agents until rollout completes.
steps: Audit current sync logging callsites in runtime and identify hot paths (inference hot loop, request router, error paths)
Design async journaling API: lock-free ring buffer sized by config, backpressure strategy (drop+metrics or block), and background flush worker with batching and compressible payloads
Implement async journal and switch logger backend behind a feature flag (runtime.env LOG_ASYNC=true) so we can toggle per-deployment
Introduce OTLP span coalescer: buffer spans for up to 10ms or N spans, compress metadata, dedupe repeated attributes, and emit a batch via grpc/http exporter
Upgrade OpenTelemetry Go SDK to v1.19.x, update exporter usage and reconcile deprecated APIs
Add end-to-end benchmarks (local harness + perf cluster) exercising bursty request patterns at varying QPS and seq length distributions
Gradual rollout: enable on internal staging, run for 72h, promote to canary region with increased sampling, then global rollout with fallback to legacy pipeline if regressions observed
Create migration docs for Dedicated and Private customers if they pin runtime flags or rely on legacy log formats
acceptance_criteria: Enable async logger behind feature flag and verify no behavioral regressions in log format or critical error routing
p99 inference tail latency reduced by >=35% on benchmark suite with bursty arrivals compared to baseline (same sequencer/weights)
CPU usage attributable to logging path reduced by >=10% under identical load
OTLP exporter emits <=60% of number of individual span RPCs in baseline by batching/coalescing without losing semantic span boundaries
No loss of user-visible error logs in 72h staging run; dropped-log metric (if configured) remains below 0.01%
Rollout plan and rollback script documented and reviewed by SRE and Security
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive buffering reduces RPCs and tail latency but increases memory pressure and can delay logs; we will expose buffer size and max-delay knobs and surface drop metrics.

We considered using an external log shipper (Fluentd) to solve tail latency but that would not address in-process blocking during log formatting; async journaling minimizes allocations and defers expensive formatting to background worker.
Span coalescer will intentionally compress repeated attribute blobs (e.g., identical model/version tags) to lower payload size; we will keep an option to expand for debugging mode.
Upgrading OTEL SDK to v1.19 requires small API changes in our exporter adapter; we've preserved a thin compatibility shim to avoid touching service integrations.
This ticket intentionally avoids changing sampling rates or higher-level rollout logic; aim is strictly perf & reliability improvements for telemetry plumbing.
